court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court-4 Mumbai at Bandra, Petition A- 438/2020
case_name: Shalini Vinesh Gayakwad vs Vinesh Tippaya Gayakwad
facts_of_case: The respondent/husband filed a petition under Section 13(1) (i-a) of the Hindu Marriage Act before the Family Court-4 Mumbai at Bandra. The applicant/wife seeks transfer of the petition to the Family Court at Akola, citing her permanent residence in Murtizapur.

legal_principles.principle: An application for transfer of a petition can be allowed if the applicant is unable to approach the court due to their permanent residence.
legal_principles.held: Considering what has been held in D. Raja Rajeswari Vs Satish Kumar (2022) 2 SCC 329, this application is allowed.
cited_cases: D. Raja Rajeswari Vs Satish Kumar, (2022) 2 SCC 329

legal_principles.principle: In case video conferencing facilities are available with the court, an application for appearing through video conferencing shall be taken into consideration.
legal_principles.held: 2. In case there is Video Conferencing facilities available with the Court at Bandra, any application filed by the non-applicant for appearing in the proceedings through video conferencing shall be taken into consideration

outcome.final_order: The application is allowed. The parties shall put an appearance before the Family Court at Akola on 12-01-2023.

keywords: D. Raja Rajeswari Vs Satish Kumar
use_for_drafting: advising on video conferencing options in family court proceedings
assisting with Hindu Marriage Act Section 13(1)(i-a) applications
